description: Hi! Our team is building “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer”: a Moon/Mars base management game where kids balance oxygen, power, food and radiation. We have: C/C++/C#/Python, ML, design & storytelling. Looking for 2 C++ devs: ideally one with game dev (raylib/SFML/SDL, simulation, ECS) and one comfortable with Emscripten/WebAssembly + build/CI so it runs in the browser. Bonus: audio, space/science nerds. English/Russian/Ukrainian. Reliable, no ghosting :)
summary: CATANAUTICS is an educational game for children aged 7–12 that turns the challenges of running a lunar base into an adventure guided by a friendly cat astronaut. Built in C++ with raylib, it combines a 3D lunar hub with four mini-games covering power distribution, water purification, radiation protection, and growing food. Players repair the base, then balance limited power and supplies to keep the crew healthy until a spacecraft arrives at the end of a three-day mission. Through accessible puzzles and resource-management decisions, the game introduces engineering trade-offs and shows how essential systems depend on one another. CATANAUTICS makes space exploration approachable while encouraging curiosity, logical thinking, and careful planning.
details:
CATANAUTICS is an educational desktop game designed for children aged 7–12. Players manage a lunar base with help from a friendly cat astronaut, learning how power, water, food, and radiation protection work together to support a crew.
The game follows a three-day mission. On Day 1, players explore a 3D lunar hub and restore four stations through different mini-games:
Power Supply Restoration: Distribute limited energy between oxygen, heating, greenhouse, and lighting systems across five checks.
Life Support Restoration: Rotate pipes to connect a water source to a reservoir, ensuring that the water passes through a filter.
Radiation Alert: Watch changing warnings and switch protection to the threatened module before a storm arrives.
Moon Greenhouse: Manage water and lighting to grow plants while avoiding drought and overwatering.
After completing all four challenges, players enter the base-management stage. On Days 2 and 3, they decide which systems receive power, build reserves, and prepare for a solar storm. Limited energy prevents every system from operating simultaneously, so players must make trade-offs. Before ending each day, they can review the consequences of their choices. The final outcome depends on the crew’s condition when the supply ship arrives.
We developed the game in C++20 using raylib, with CMake for building and Git/GitHub for version control and distribution. The project combines a 3D hub with 2D interfaces and includes an executable build for Windows x64.
Our creative approach pairs a playful cat astronaut and a bright yellow-and-purple visual style with resource-management decisions. Different mechanics—sliders, pipe puzzles, timed switching, and plant care—give players several ways to explore the mission’s challenges.
The team focused on readable interfaces, straightforward controls, clear feedback, and a complete story with an achievable goal. Scientific concepts are presented through simplified game rules rather than as a realistic engineering simulation. Our intended impact is to encourage curiosity about space, develop planning and prioritization skills, and help young learners understand why successful missions depend on balancing interconnected systems.
